title: DepEd’s AI tool to catch early learning deficiencies
summary: Within 15 minutes, the newly developed artificial intelligence tool of the Department of Education can assess learners who are at risk of learning and communication difficulties.

blocks.text: In a statement yesterday, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said that through their Project SABAY or Screening using AI-Based Assistance for Young Children, they would be able to screen Grade 2 learners for risks of learning and communication difficulties, which is an improvement over traditional methods that can take up to two hours per learner.

MANILA, Philippines — Within 15 minutes, the newly developed artificial intelligence (AI) tool of the Department of Education (DepEd) can assess learners who are at risk of learning and communication difficulties.
He said the AI-based tool is meant to empower educators and give parents clear insights to support their child’s development.

“By providing them with transparent, data-driven tools that show step-by-step results, we are giving our teachers the confidence and clarity they need to partner effectively with parents and secure early interventions,” he said.

The AI app was developed by the Bureau of Learning Delivery and the Education Center for AI Research. It transforms the typically tedious screening process into an engaging, story-driven experience that makes young children feel comfortable and stress-free.

Through a teacher-assisted application, learners complete gamified speech tasks such as picture naming, word dictation, nonsense word dictation and spontaneous vocalization. Its interactive format makes screening more natural and less stressful for young learners.

School heads and teachers have also praised the platform’s transparency, noting that its step-by-step analytical breakdown helps them clearly explain screening results to parents and build stronger partnerships for learner intervention.
The system also addresses a critical bottleneck in the country’s health care and educational support network.

After its initial pilot testing in the National Capital Region, DepEd has expanded data collection across the Visayas, Mindanao and upcoming regions in Luzon to ensure the AI tool adapts effectively to the country’s diverse cultural and linguistic landscape.
P440 million sought for more counselors

The Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2) yesterday advocated for an additional allocation of P440 million for 1,100 school counselor associate positions in the national budget for 2027, on top of the 3,000 SCA positions included in the proposed budget.

EDCOM 2 cited the 2022 Program for International Student Assessment data where 43 percent of Filipino girls and 53 percent of boys were reported being bullied a few times a month, with rates roughly twice the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development average.

The 2024 Southeast Asia Primary Learning Metrics also discovered that 50 percent of Filipino Grade 5 learners experienced bullying at least once a month, which is reportedly the highest rate in Southeast Asia.
